samples.summary: New defensive filtering of malformed `usedControls` entries has no test
samples.evidence: The change adds two guards for junk in `usedControls`: `mergeCoverage` filters `typeof n === "string" && n !== ""` (hunt-ui-coverage.mjs:407) and `renderCoverageBrief` filters the same (hunt-ui-coverage.mjs:492-494). The file's dedicated robustness test, "a malformed record degrades to empty coverage instead of killing the run" (test.mjs:299-323), builds `withJunk` with junk in `shapes`, `pairs` and `readAfterMutation` but NOT `usedControls`; no other test passes a non-string/empty entry (e.g. `usedControls: [null, 7, "", {}]`) or a non-array `usedControls`. So both new filters could be deleted and the whole suite would still be green — the coverage for them is nominal only.
searchedFor: grep mergeCoverage|renderCoverageBrief call sites in scripts/agent/hunt-ui.mjs

samples.summary: Only the `prev` side of the `usedControls` union is exercised; the `next` side and the normal (non-bump) merge are untested
samples.evidence: `mergeCoverage` unions four sources (hunt-ui-coverage.mjs:401-408): prev.usedControls, next.usedControls, prev.shapes, next.shapes. The two new merge tests both put the surviving data on `prev` — test.mjs:193-208 (stale prev shapes) and test.mjs:220-221 (stale prev usedControls) — and the `next` argument carries no `usedControls` in either. Dropping the `next?.usedControls` and `next.shapes` terms would leave every test passing (the loader path `mergeCoverage(null, record)` at hunt-ui.mjs:1166 puts the record in `next`, so that is the production shape that is unasserted). Likewise no test asserts `usedControls` on a merge of two current-version records (test.mjs:169-185 asserts only `shapes`), nor that duplicates are deduped.
searchedFor: inspected mergeCoverage call sites in scripts/agent/hunt-ui.mjs:1166,1403
